stem: A 25-year-old has years of scanty, foul-smelling ear discharge with progressive hearing loss; otoscopy shows a retraction pocket and perforation in the attic (pars flaccida) filled with white pearly debris. Why is this type of chronic otitis media termed 'unsafe'?
options: The keratinising squamous epithelium (cholesteatoma) erodes bone and can cause facial palsy or intracranial complications
It always resolves spontaneously without treatment
It is purely a cosmetic problem of the pinna
concept: An attic (pars flaccida) retraction/perforation with foul scanty discharge and pearly debris indicates a cholesteatoma - a sac of keratinising squamous epithelium that releases bone-eroding enzymes; it is the 'unsafe' (atticoantral) type of CSOM because it can erode the ossicles, facial canal, labyrinth and tegmen, causing facial palsy, labyrinthitis and intracranial abscess, and needs surgery (mastoidectomy). The 'safe' (tubotympanic) type has a central perforation with mucoid discharge.
reference: Dhingra, Diseases of Ear, Nose and Throat
subject: ENT
